- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 85+), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “rebound” or “mean reversion” effect.
- Model underestimates when true price drops below 75, particularly in the middle-to-late horizon (e.g., 70–72 range), suggesting it underweights downward momentum.
- Model shows persistent bias toward higher prices in the first 10–15 days, then gradually drifts lower — may be overfitting to recent high prices.
- Model often fails to adjust for seasonal or calendar-driven patterns (e.g., price dips around mid-November), suggesting it lacks context-awareness.
- Forecasts are too smooth — fail to capture volatility clustering or sudden reversals — especially after 70–75 price zones.
- Model underestimates true price when it’s trending downward from a peak — may be missing “selloff” or “bearish momentum” signals.
- Model tends to overcorrect after a sharp drop — e.g., after 70–72, it often forecasts a rebound too aggressively, then fails to adjust downward again.
- Model is sensitive to recent high prices — overweights recent spikes, underweights long-term mean — may need to incorporate moving average or volatility-adjusted smoothing.
